column1: # docs/globals-ratchet.tsv -- the RATCHET CEILINGS for plan_globals.md.
# Same convention as docs/shim-ratchet.tsv, and for the same reason: every
# number here is a CEILING re-measured FROM THE TREE on each test run. The test
# that reads this file is
#   sourcesharp/test/globals_ledger_test.cpp
# and it FAILS when a measured number goes ABOVE its ceiling. Going below is the
# whole point of the plan and needs no ceremony beyond lowering the row.
# NOTHING HERE IS A KEEP-LIST. This file holds only counts; the per-symbol
# rulings live in docs/globals-ledger.tsv, which the gate re-derives against the
# symbol table on every run. A list of names nobody re-derives rots silently.
# HOW TO CHANGE IT
#   you made a number smaller   lower the row, in the same commit
#   you made a number BIGGER    that is the regression this file exists to
#                               catch. Raising a row is a deliberate act: say
#                               in the commit message what came back and why.
# MERGING TWO LANES' VERSIONS: do not keep both. Re-measure against the merged
# tree and write the number you measured.
# columns:
# metric
# THE LEDGER MUST COVER THE SYMBOL TABLE, BOTH WAYS.
# These two are the membership gate and both ceilings are ZERO, which is the
# point: a ceiling of zero fails on the first row in either direction.
#   globals_symbols_with_no_row   a piece of state nobody has written down.
#   globals_rows_with_no_symbol   a row describing a tree that no longer
#                                 exists. This is the direction a keep-list
#                                 rots in, and it is the one that was caught at
#                                 a merge on this project on 2026-09-20: a row
#                                 naming a file deleted three phases earlier
#                                 still read as a live claim because nothing

# THE ROWS NOBODY HAS RULED. UNRULED is an admission, not a disposition: the
# symbol has a ledger row so the membership gate passes, but no human has read
# it and said where it goes. This is the number the plan exists to drive to
# zero, and it is the one row here that is a statement about POLICY rather than
# about size -- the same shape as `shim_reason_none` in docs/shim-ratchet.tsv.

# headers, s_gameShellDll, the two stock static-init chains the engine walks,
# and the compiler's own DW.ref. MEMBER, MANAGED and CONST are left to the
# steps that read the code.

# derived source -- a link-line object, an archive (`nm` over the .a files,

# "in the .so and not in an object", which made the identity true by
# construction -- a check that could not fail, and this project has counted
# more than fifty of those.

#             436 + 129 archive + 14 crt = 579 = so_mutable        AGREE
#   release   453 - 29 dropped = 424
